title: Grateful Dead Live at Paramount Northwest Theater on 1972-07-21
lineage: Dat (Sony PCM-R500)(16/48) > Tascam DA-3000 (16/48)> Adobe Audition CC 2019 > TLH flac1648
source: Bear's Master Soundboard Cassettes > 1st generation Cassettes > 2nd generation Cassettes > Tim Dalton's Dat (16/48)

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a smoking 1972 show highlighted by an epic ‘Other One’ and intense Stella Blue moments.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as a “significant upgrade” over comparable releases, delivering crisp soundboard clarity with a balanced mix that lets the instruments breathe. Musically the concert is described as a “G‑R‑A‑T‑E” performance – mellow yet tight first set and a high‑energy second set featuring a 22‑minute smoking ‘The Other One’, towering ‘Truckin’ outro, and an intense standalone Stella Blue. Overall the show is celebrated for its apex‑level band interplay and strong vocal contributions.

ai_rating.rationale: The reviewer gives a perfect 5‑star rating, lauds both the musical performance (standout jams, high energy) and the recording quality (significant upgrade, clear mix). With detailed comments across many songs and technical aspects, confidence in the rating is high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as a ‘significant upgrade’ with crisp clarity; drum kit sits well in the mix, no major dropouts or muffiness noted.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Mellow, vocal‑rich first set that builds into a high‑octane second set; transitions such as WRS prelude > Me & My Uncle and the seamless Truckin → Drums → Other One → Comes a Time sequence are highlighted.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is praised throughout, especially on ‘Stella Blue’, ‘Deal’, and the soaring lead in ‘Truckin’ and ‘The Other One’.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s backing vocals are highlighted on ‘Mexicali’, ‘I Know You Rider’, and he adds an “x‑factor” to several numbers; his bass work is noted as solid during the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s exploratory playing is mentioned positively, noting it’s good to hear him tinkering and exploring.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (Mickey) isn’t overly prominent in the mix but provides a solid journey; no over‑the‑top solos, just tasteful support.
